patch.value: Cross-process real-time bus so pm-gpt/pm-mcp edits reach pm-web SSE clients (and scale across replicas)

FINDING (2026-07-11 hosted-services audit): pm-web already has SSE real-time (services/sse.ts: broadcastProjectEvent + presence), but the client registry is an in-memory per-process array (clients: SSEClient[]). There is NO cross-process propagation (no LISTEN/NOTIFY, Redis, or fs.watch). Consequences for the hosted stack (pm-web + pm-gpt + pm-mcp all share the pm-cli_pm-web-projects volume + Postgres): (1) an edit made via ChatGPT/pm-gpt writes the shared volume directly and does NOT trigger a pm-web SSE broadcast, so pm-web UI users only see it on manual refresh; (2) horizontally scaling pm-web to serve thousands of concurrent users breaks live updates because SSE clients on replica A never receive events broadcast on replica B. Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY is the natural fix (shared dep, no new infra). This is the gap between 'has real-time' and 'multi-user real-time live collaboration across all connected services'.

SSE broadcasts propagate across processes/replicas via Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (Postgres is already a shared dependency — no new infra). On any pm item create/update/close — whether made by pm-web itself, pm-gpt (ChatGPT), or pm-mcp writing to the shared PROJECTS_ROOT volume — a NOTIFY is emitted; every pm-web instance LISTENs and re-broadcasts to its local SSE clients (item events + presence). Writes that bypass the pm-web API (direct file writes on the shared volume) are still surfaced (via a NOTIFY hook or a lightweight change-detector). Verified: an edit via pm-gpt appears in a pm-web UI SSE stream in real time; two pm-web instances sharing the DB both deliver the same event. No data loss; no regression to single-process behavior.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: Implementing the two remaining acceptance items on branch feat/external-change-detector-realtime. (1) LIGHTWEIGHT CHANGE-DETECTOR for out-of-band direct writes to the shared PROJECTS_ROOT volume: polls ONLY projects that currently have SSE clients (scales with live viewership, avoids inotify/node_modules watch explosion; extensions/pm-graph/node_modules has ~2700 files per project). Maps projectId->dir via cached DB lookup (pm_projects.id -> user_id+slug -> PROJECTS_ROOT/<userId>/<slug>), scans item .toon + history .jsonl mtimes (excludes extensions/runtime/locks/search/index), emits local 'workspace-changed' (client already refreshes on it, silent — no userId => no toast). SUPPRESSES changes already signaled via deliverProjectEvent (pm-web API writes + pm-gpt NOTIFYs both flow through it) using a wall-clock window > poll interval, so no doubling of SSE traffic at scale. (2) TWO-REPLICA DELIVERY TEST: minimal realtime-bus refactor exporting pure buildEnvelope/handleIncomingEnvelope so a test proves a message published by replica A is delivered by replica B and self-skipped by A — infra-free (CI has no Postgres). Confirmed: pm-gpt==pm-mcp writes directly + pg_notify (workspaces.ts:123); hosted pm-web built from public ./fleet/pm-web via companion compose.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text:
Bot-review hardening round (PR #56, CodeRabbit + Sourcery):
- CodeRabbit Major (project-watcher.ts): a reduced max(mtime) missed mtime-preserving restores (files rewritten with OLDER preserved mtimes never advance the max) and same-instant add/remove. Replaced with a composite signature `count:max:sum(mtime BigInt)` computed in the same stat pass (zero extra I/O); emit switched from emit-on-increase to emit-on-change. Real-filesystem functional test confirms an older-mtime restore is now detected while extensions/node_modules churn stays ignored. The >8000-file cap remains a documented backstop (bounded round-robin scan tracked as follow-up).
- CodeRabbit + Sourcery (both flagged): defaultResolveProjectDir swallowed transient DB errors and cached null for the whole SSE session, permanently silencing the watcher for that project. Now DB errors propagate to onError (retried next tick); only genuine misses/successes are cached. New unit test proves throw-then-retry.
- Sourcery test suggestions: added realtime-bus tests for non-plain-object data normalizing to {} and whitelist/length bounding (which is WHY buildEnvelope can never approach the 7.5KB cap — the oversized-through-buildEnvelope path is unreachable by construction).
Verified: typecheck + build clean, 121/121 tests (was 117), audit:prod 0 vulns, changelog:check up to date.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text:
Bot-review round 2 (PR #56, CodeRabbit deep re-review — 2 new Major findings, both fixed):
- COLLISION (project-watcher.ts): raw count:max:sum(mtime) aliases distinct states ({100,200,300} vs {150,150,300} share count/max/sum). Replaced with a PATH-KEYED fingerprint: per file h=fnv1a32("<subdir>/<name>:<mtimeMs>") combined order-independently via XOR+sum (same stat pass, Number math, no BigInt-per-byte). Rearranging mtimes across paths now changes the fingerprint. Exported computeWorkspaceSignature + added a real-tmpdir unit test proving the two aggregate-colliding arrangements yield DISTINCT signatures.
- SUPPRESSION CORRELATION (project-watcher.ts + sse.ts): the timestamp-only suppress window swallowed ANY fs delta while signaled, so an UNRELATED direct edit landing within a realtime event's window was consumed and never emitted. Added sse.consumeSignaledMutation(); the watcher now attributes exactly ONE delta to a signal then consumes it — a later unrelated direct edit finds no signal and emits. New unit test covers the interleave (signal→suppress+consume→later edit emits). Residual: two writes aggregating into a SINGLE <2s tick can't be split (documented; acceptable — emit-cost is a silent refresh).
- DEFERRED (>8000-file cap, project-watcher.ts:34): bounded round-robin scan for eventual coverage of very large projects filed as pm-web-acwm (backstop-only; primary paths = API broadcast + pg_notify).
Verified: build clean, 123/123 tests (was 117 at PR open), functional real-fs test PASS, audit:prod 0 vulns, changelog:check up to date.
